narrative:
**Engagement surged across the board, led by Spaces.** Space likes more than doubled week over week, rising 148.2% to 2,527 across the 7,146 Spaces in scope (up 45.2% versus four weeks ago). Model downloads rose 60.5% to 5.73M across 25,072 models, a 20.1% gain on the four-week baseline, while model likes rose 12.9% to 12,654 but were essentially flat on a four-week view (+0.3%). The divergence between the one-week and four-week deltas on downloads and likes suggests a single-week spike rather than a sustained step change; the Spaces universe itself also grew, so part of the likes increase reflects a larger denominator.

**Qwen tightened its grip on coding while the model-family picture stayed thinly covered.** Among the 135 coding Spaces, Qwen held 45.2% share (+16.3% w/w), with proprietary APIs falling to 5.9% (-31.4%) and Llama to 3.7% (-26.5%). In the much larger chat-assistant segment (664 Spaces), Qwen slipped to 25.2% (-9.9%) as DeepSeek rose to 5.3% (+44.8%) and proprietary APIs to 12.3% (+25.0%); "other-open" remained the plurality at 42.0%. Counts by family fell for most named families — Qwen 4,650 (-16.0%), Llama 950 (-10.3%), Gemma 595 (-22.0%), DeepSeek 215 (-49.8% w/w, though still +78.3% on four weeks) — while GLM/Zhipu rose to 137 (+39.8%) and Nemotron to 199 (+11.2%). An important caveat: 12,537 of 25,072 models (50.0%) were unclassified as "unknown," and that bucket grew 5.9% w/w, so family-share movements should be read as directional only. Several use-case cells are also very small (robotics had 13 Spaces, 3D-gaming 41, music-generation 31), where a single Space moves share by several points — the robotics and 3D-gaming swings are too thin to interpret.

**On capability and vertical mix, inference-side and document workloads gained.** Local-inference penetration rose to 2.73% of Spaces (+13.8%) and quantization to 2.55% (+12.9%), while multimodal (5.42%, -6.9%), vision-language (6.33%, -5.4%) and tool-use (3.15%, -5.2%) eased; long-context remained a very small base at 0.39%, so its +64.4% move is noise-prone. By use case, document-AI Spaces rose 23.0% to 545 and chat-assistant 10.5% to 1,125, against a 33.3% drop in scientific-tools to 230 and a 10.7% drop in video-generation to 343. Verticals showed cybersecurity up 19.9% to 2.50% penetration and consumer up 16.9% to 10.72%, with industrial-manufacturing (-17.5%) and scientific-research (-14.3%) down. Next week, watch whether the download and Space-like spikes persist or revert toward the four-week trend, and whether the scientific-tools decline continues.
